name: Jeroham
who: A priest, father of Adaiah, whose family line traced back through Pashhur to Malchijah.
key: Adaiah son of Jeroham, of Pashhur's line, lived in Jerusalem after the exile (1 Chronicles 9).
Nehemiah gives his line as Jeroham son of Pelaliah, descended from Pashhur and Malchijah (Nehemiah 11).

name: Jeshaiah
who: A Benjaminite, father of Ithiel and earliest named ancestor of Sallu, who settled in Jerusalem after the exile.
key: Sallu son of Meshullam is traced through Joed, Pedaiah, Kolaiah, Maaseiah, and Ithiel to Jeshaiah (Nehemiah 11).
These Benjaminites were among the people who lived in Jerusalem, the holy city (Nehemiah 11).

name: Jeshaiah
who: A Levite of the sons of Merari who came with Hashabiah from Casiphia to join Ezra's return.
key: Ezra sent to Iddo at Casiphia for ministers for the house of God (Ezra 8).
Hashabiah came, and with him Jeshaiah of the sons of Merari, with twenty of their kinsmen (Ezra 8).

name: Jeshishai
who: A Gadite, son of Jahdo and father of Michael, in the ancestry of Abihail's family.
key: Abihail's line runs through Michael son of Jeshishai, son of Jahdo, son of Buz (1 Chronicles 5).
These Gadites lived in Gilead, in Bashan, and in the pasturelands of Sharon (1 Chronicles 5).

name: Jeshua
who: Head of a family within the clan of Pahath-moab whose descendants returned from exile with Zerubbabel.
key: His descendants, with Joab's, were counted among the sons of Pahath-moab, numbering 2,812 (Ezra 2).
Nehemiah's copy of the list gives 2,818 for the same families (Nehemiah 7).

name: Jeshua
who: Levite leader after the exile who helped rebuild the temple and teach the Law in Ezra and Nehemiah's day.
key: Levites of the family of Jeshua and Kadmiel returned from exile with Zerubbabel (Ezra 2).
Jeshua and his sons supervised the workmen rebuilding the temple (Ezra 3).

name: Jeshua
who: A chief of the Levites after the exile, son of Kadmiel, who led praise and thanksgiving.
key: Jeshua son of Kadmiel is named among the chiefs of the Levites (Nehemiah 12).
With their brothers they stood in sections to praise and give thanks, as David commanded (Nehemiah 12).

name: Jeshua
who: The high priest, son of Jozadak, who returned from exile with Zerubbabel and helped rebuild the temple.
key: He was among the leaders who returned from Babylon with Zerubbabel (Ezra 2).
He and his fellow priests rebuilt the altar and began laying the temple's foundation (Ezra 3).

name: Jesse
who: A man of Bethlehem, grandson of Boaz and Ruth, and the father of King David.
key: Jesse is named as the son of Obed and grandson of Boaz and Ruth (Ruth 4).
Samuel anointed Jesse's youngest son David as the future king (1 Samuel 16).

name: Jesus
who: The Son of God and promised Messiah, born of Mary, who died for sinners and rose again.
key: He was born of the virgin Mary in Bethlehem and laid in a manger (Luke 2).
He was baptized by John and then tempted by the devil in the wilderness (Matthew 3–4).

name: Jether
who: The husband of David's sister Abigail and father of Amasa, called Jether the Ishmaelite and also Ithra.
key: Amasa, whom Absalom set over his army, was the son of Ithra and Abigail (2 Samuel 17).
David reminded Solomon how Joab had killed Amasa the son of Jether (1 Kings 2).

name: Jethro
who: Priest of Midian and father-in-law of Moses, who gave Moses wise counsel in the wilderness.
key: Moses helped his daughters at a well and later married his daughter Zipporah (Exodus 2).
Moses was keeping his flock when God spoke from the burning bush (Exodus 3).

name: Jeush
who: A Benjaminite, son of Bilhan, whose family was counted among Benjamin's mighty warriors.
key: The sons of Bilhan were Jeush, Benjamin, Ehud, Chenaanah, Zethan, Tarshish, and Ahishahar (1 Chronicles 7).
They were heads of fathers' houses, mighty warriors, 17,200 able to go to war (1 Chronicles 7).

name: Jeush
who: A son of King Rehoboam by Mahalath, a granddaughter of David.
key: Mahalath bore Rehoboam sons: Jeush, Shemariah, and Zaham (2 Chronicles 11).
Rehoboam later made Maacah's son Abijah chief prince among his brothers (2 Chronicles 11).

name: Jeush
who: A son of Esau and Oholibamah, born in Canaan, who became a chief in Edom.
key: Oholibamah bore Jeush to Esau in Canaan, along with Jalam and Korah (Genesis 36).
He became one of the chiefs descended from Esau (Genesis 36).

name: Jezebel
who: Sidonian princess who married King Ahab of Israel and promoted Baal worship.
key: Ahab married her and began to serve and worship Baal (1 Kings 16).
She killed the prophets of the LORD and supported hundreds of Baal's prophets (1 Kings 18).

name: Jezreel
who: The first son of the prophet Hosea and Gomer, whose name announced judgment and later restoration.
key: Gomer bore Hosea a son, and the LORD told him to name the boy Jezreel (Hosea 1).
The name announced punishment on Jehu's house for the blood shed at Jezreel (Hosea 1).

name: Joab
who: Son of David's sister Zeruiah and the commander of David's army.
key: He led the attack on Jerusalem and became chief commander (1 Chronicles 11).
He murdered Abner in revenge for his brother Asahel's death (2 Samuel 3).

name: Joah
who: A son of Asaph who served as recorder under King Hezekiah of Judah.
key: He went out with Eliakim and Shebna to meet the Assyrian Rabshakeh (2 Kings 18).
They asked the Rabshakeh to speak in Aramaic rather than in Hebrew (2 Kings 18).

name: Joash
who: Abiezrite of Ophrah, father of Gideon, who defended his son after Gideon tore down Baal's altar.
key: The angel of the LORD appeared to Gideon under the terebinth at Ophrah belonging to Joash (Judges 6).
When the town demanded Gideon's death, Joash said Baal should contend for himself (Judges 6).

name: Joash
who: King of Judah, rescued as an infant, who repaired the temple but later turned from the LORD.
key: His aunt Jehosheba hid him in the temple for six years from Athaliah (2 Kings 11).
At age seven he was crowned king by the priest Jehoiada (2 Kings 11).

name: Joash
who: A king of Israel, son of Jehoahaz and father of Jeroboam II.
key: Joash became king of Israel in Samaria and did evil (2 Kings 13).
He wept over the dying Elisha and struck the ground with arrows (2 Kings 13).

name: Job
who: A blameless and upright man from Uz who suffered great loss yet did not curse God.
key: Satan was allowed to test him, and he lost his livestock, servants, and children (Job 1).
Struck with painful sores, he refused to curse God (Job 2).

name: Jobab
who: A son of Joktan in Shem's line, named in the Table of Nations.
key: Jobab is listed among the thirteen sons of Joktan, with Ophir and Havilah (Genesis 10).
Chronicles repeats him among the descendants of Shem through Eber (1 Chronicles 1).

name: Jobab
who: An early king of Edom, son of Zerah of Bozrah, who reigned before Israel had kings.
key: Jobab son of Zerah of Bozrah reigned in Edom after Bela died (Genesis 36).
When Jobab died, Husham of the land of the Temanites reigned in his place (Genesis 36).

name: Jochebed
who: A daughter of Levi, wife of Amram, and mother of Aaron, Moses, and Miriam.
key: As Moses' mother, she hid her baby for three months from Pharaoh's decree (Exodus 2).
She placed him in a basket among the reeds by the Nile (Exodus 2).

name: Joed
who: A Benjaminite, son of Pedaiah and father of Meshullam, in the ancestry of Sallu of Jerusalem.
key: Sallu son of Meshullam, son of Joed, son of Pedaiah, settled in Jerusalem (Nehemiah 11).
Joed's line is traced back through Kolaiah, Maaseiah, Ithiel, and Jeshaiah (Nehemiah 11).

name: Joel
who: Samuel's firstborn son, a corrupt judge in Beersheba, and father of the singer Heman.
key: Samuel appointed his sons Joel and Abijah as judges in Beersheba (1 Samuel 8).
They turned aside after gain, took bribes, and perverted justice (1 Samuel 8).

name: Joel
who: A Reubenite whose descendants, including Baal and the exiled chief Beerah, are listed in Chronicles.
key: The sons of Joel are traced through Shemaiah, Gog, Shimei, Micah, Reaiah, and Baal (1 Chronicles 5).
His descendant Beerah, a Reubenite chief, was exiled by Tiglath-pileser of Assyria (1 Chronicles 5).

name: Joel
who: Brother of Nathan, named among David's mighty men in Chronicles.
key: Joel the brother of Nathan is listed among the mighty men of David's army (1 Chronicles 11).
These warriors gave David strong support in his kingdom, with all Israel (1 Chronicles 11).

name: Joel
who: A Gershonite Levite of the family of Ladan who helped oversee the temple treasuries.
key: He is listed with Jehiel and Zetham among the sons of Ladan (1 Chronicles 23).
With his brother Zetham he was in charge of the treasuries of the house of the LORD (1 Chronicles 26).

name: Joel
who: A Benjaminite, son of Zichri, overseer of the Benjaminites who settled in Jerusalem after the exile.
key: Gabbai and Sallai and 928 Benjaminites lived in Jerusalem (Nehemiah 11).
Joel son of Zichri was their overseer, and Judah son of Hassenuah was second over the city (Nehemiah 11).

name: Joel
who: A prophet, son of Pethuel, who used a locust plague to call Judah to repentance.
key: The word of the LORD came to Joel son of Pethuel (Joel 1).
He called priests and people to mourn and fast after a devastating locust plague (Joel 1).

name: Joha
who: A Benjaminite, son of Beriah, named among the family heads of Benjamin who lived in Jerusalem.
key: Michael, Ispah, and Joha are named among the sons of Beriah (1 Chronicles 8).
Beriah and Shema, heads in Aijalon, had put the inhabitants of Gath to flight (1 Chronicles 8).

name: Johanan
who: Son of Kareah and a Judean army captain who led the remnant to Egypt after Jerusalem fell.
key: He warned Governor Gedaliah that Ishmael planned to kill him (Jeremiah 40).
He rescued the captives Ishmael had taken from Mizpah (Jeremiah 41).

name: Johanan
who: A descendant of David's royal line after the exile, one of the seven sons of Elioenai.
key: The sons of Elioenai were Hodaviah, Eliashib, Pelaiah, Akkub, Johanan, Delaiah, and Anani, seven (1 Chronicles 3).
His family belonged to the royal line of Zerubbabel and King Jehoiachin (1 Chronicles 3).

name: Johanan
who: A priest in Aaron's high priestly line, son of Azariah and father of Azariah.
key: He is listed in the high priestly line as son of Azariah, grandson of Ahimaaz (1 Chronicles 6).
His son Azariah served as priest in the house Solomon built in Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 6).

name: Johanan
who: A high priest after the exile, named in the high-priestly succession between Joiada and Jaddua.
key: Levite family heads were recorded in the days of Eliashib, Joiada, Johanan, and Jaddua (Nehemiah 12).
The Levites' heads were written in the Book of the Chronicles until the days of Johanan son of Eliashib (Nehemiah 12).

name: John the Baptist
who: Prophet, son of Zechariah and Elizabeth, who prepared the way for Jesus and baptized him.
key: An angel announced his birth to his father Zechariah in the temple (Luke 1).
He preached repentance in the wilderness and baptized people in the Jordan (Matthew 3).

name: John
who: A fisherman, son of Zebedee and brother of James, who became one of Jesus' twelve apostles.
key: Jesus called John and James from mending nets with their father (Matthew 4; Mark 1).
Jesus named John and James Boanerges, meaning Sons of Thunder (Mark 3).

name: John
who: A member of the high priest's family who sat on the council that questioned Peter and John.
key: He gathered with Annas, Caiaphas, and Alexander to question Peter and John after a lame man was healed (Acts 4).
The council, unable to deny the miracle, warned the apostles and released them (Acts 4).

name: Joiada
who: A high priest after the exile, son of Eliashib, whose son married Sanballat's daughter.
key: He is listed in the high priestly line as son of Eliashib and father of Jonathan (Nehemiah 12).
Levite family heads were recorded in the days of Eliashib, Joiada, Johanan, and Jaddua (Nehemiah 12).

name: Joiakim
who: A high priest after the exile, son of Jeshua and father of Eliashib.
key: Jeshua fathered Joiakim, and Joiakim fathered Eliashib in the high-priestly line (Nehemiah 12).
In Joiakim's days the heads of the priestly fathers' houses were recorded (Nehemiah 12).

name: Jokshan
who: A son of Abraham by Keturah and the father of Sheba and Dedan.
key: Keturah bore Jokshan and five other sons to Abraham (Genesis 25).
Jokshan fathered Sheba and Dedan; Dedan's descendants included the Asshurim and Letushim (Genesis 25).

name: Joktan
who: A son of Eber and brother of Peleg, ancestor of thirteen Arabian peoples.
key: He was born to Eber, and his brother Peleg was named for the earth's division (Genesis 10).
He fathered thirteen sons, including Sheba, Ophir, and Havilah (Genesis 10).

name: Jonadab
who: A nephew of David and a very crafty friend of Amnon.
key: He was the son of David's brother Shimeah and a friend of Amnon (2 Samuel 13).
He advised Amnon to pretend illness so Tamar would come to him (2 Samuel 13).

name: Jonadab
who: Son of Rechab who supported Jehu against Baal worship and gave his descendants strict rules of life.
key: Jehu took him into his chariot to see his zeal for the LORD (2 Kings 10).
He went with Jehu into the house of Baal before Baal's worshipers were destroyed (2 Kings 10).

name: Jonah
who: A prophet of Israel, son of Amittai, sent by God to preach to Nineveh.
key: Jonah foretold the restoration of Israel's borders under Jeroboam II (2 Kings 14).
Fleeing God's call, he was thrown overboard and swallowed by a great fish (Jonah 1).

name: Jonathan
who: A grandson of Moses through Gershom who became priest to the tribe of Dan's carved image.
key: He is apparently the young Levite whom Micah hired as priest for his household shrine (Judges 17).
The Danites took Micah's image and priest and set them up in their new city of Dan (Judges 18).

name: Jonathan
who: Eldest son of King Saul, a brave warrior, and David's loyal friend.
key: With only his armor-bearer, he attacked a Philistine garrison, and God gave victory (1 Samuel 14).
He made a covenant with David and gave him his robe and weapons (1 Samuel 18).

name: Jonathan
who: A son of the priest Abiathar who served as a messenger for David during Absalom's revolt.
key: David sent him back to Jerusalem with Ahimaaz to bring him word (2 Samuel 15).
Hiding in a well at Bahurim, he escaped and warned David to cross the Jordan (2 Samuel 17).

name: Jonathan
who: One of David's mighty men, a son of Shagee the Hararite.
key: He is listed among David's elite warriors known as the thirty (2 Samuel 23).
Chronicles names him Jonathan son of Shagee the Hararite among David's mighty men (1 Chronicles 11).

name: Jonathan
who: A son of Kareah and brother of Johanan, an army captain in Judah after Jerusalem fell.
key: After Babylon took Jerusalem, he and Johanan came with their men to Gedaliah at Mizpah (Jeremiah 40).
Gedaliah urged these captains to serve the king of Babylon and settle in the land (Jeremiah 40).

name: Jorai
who: A Gadite, one of the seven sons of Abihail who headed fathers' houses in Gilead and Bashan.
key: Abihail's sons Michael, Meshullam, Sheba, Jorai, Jacan, Zia, and Eber headed their fathers' houses (1 Chronicles 5).
These Gadites lived in Gilead, in Bashan and its towns, and in the pasturelands of Sharon (1 Chronicles 5).

name: Joram
who: A son of Toi king of Hamath, sent to congratulate David on his victory over Hadadezer.
key: Toi sent his son Joram to greet and congratulate King David for defeating Hadadezer (2 Samuel 8).
Joram brought articles of silver, gold, and bronze, which David dedicated to the LORD (2 Samuel 8).

name: Joram
who: King of Israel, son of Ahab and Jezebel, who was killed by Jehu.
key: He became king of Israel after his brother Ahaziah died without a son (2 Kings 1).
With Jehoshaphat he fought Moab, and Elisha foretold God's supply of water (2 Kings 3).

name: Jehozadak
who: A priest, son of Seraiah, taken into exile by Nebuchadnezzar and father of Joshua the high priest.
key: He went into exile when the Lord sent Judah and Jerusalem away by Nebuchadnezzar (1 Chronicles 6).
His son Jeshua led the priests in rebuilding the altar after the return (Ezra 3).

name: Joseph
who: Favored son of Jacob and Rachel, sold into slavery by his brothers, who rose to rule Egypt.
key: Jacob's favorite, he dreamed of ruling his brothers, who sold him into slavery (Genesis 37).
Falsely accused by Potiphar's wife, he was thrown into prison (Genesis 39).

name: Joseph
who: A man of the tribe of Issachar, father of Igal, one of the twelve spies.
key: His son Igal represented Issachar among the twelve men Moses sent to spy out Canaan (Numbers 13).
Igal was among the spies who brought back a bad report of the land (Numbers 13).

name: Joseph
who: Carpenter of Nazareth from David's line, husband of Mary and legal father of Jesus.
key: An angel told him in a dream to take Mary as his wife (Matthew 1).
He went to Bethlehem for the census, where Jesus was born (Luke 2).

name: Joseph of Arimathea
who: A rich council member and disciple of Jesus who buried Jesus' body in his own new tomb.
key: A rich disciple from Arimathea, he laid Jesus in his own new rock tomb (Matthew 27).
A respected council member, he boldly asked Pilate for Jesus' body (Mark 15).

name: Joses
who: One of the brothers of Jesus, named with James, Simon, and Judas by the people of Nazareth.
key: The people of Nazareth named Joses among Jesus' brothers when they took offense at him (Matthew 13).
Mark also lists Joses with James, Judas, and Simon as brothers of Jesus (Mark 6).

name: Joshua
who: Son of Nun, Moses' assistant and successor, who led Israel into the Promised Land.
key: He led Israel's army to victory over Amalek while Moses held up his hands (Exodus 17).
With Caleb, he was one of two spies who urged Israel to trust God (Numbers 13–14).

name: Joshua
who: High priest who returned from Babylon with Zerubbabel and helped lead the rebuilding of the temple.
key: He returned from exile with Zerubbabel among the first group of exiles (Ezra 2).
He and Zerubbabel rebuilt the altar and laid the temple's foundation (Ezra 3).

name: Josiah
who: Godly king of Judah, son of Amon, who led sweeping reforms after the Book of the Law was found.
key: A man of God foretold by name that Josiah would destroy the altar at Bethel (1 Kings 13).
He became king at eight, and the Book of the Law was found during temple repairs (2 Kings 22).

name: Jotham
who: The youngest son of Gideon, the only brother to escape Abimelech's massacre.
key: He survived by hiding when Abimelech killed his seventy brothers on one stone (Judges 9).
From Mount Gerizim he told Shechem's leaders a fable about the trees choosing a king (Judges 9).

name: Jotham
who: King of Judah, son of Uzziah, who did what was right and grew strong.
key: He governed the people while his father Uzziah lived in isolation with leprosy (2 Kings 15).
He became king at twenty-five and reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem (2 Chronicles 27).

name: Jozabad
who: One of two men named Jozabad among Manasseh's commanders who deserted to David.
key: As David went to Ziklag, he joined David as a chief of thousands in Manasseh (1 Chronicles 12).
These men helped David against the band of raiders and became commanders in his army (1 Chronicles 12).

name: Jozabad
who: One of two men named Jozabad among Manasseh's commanders who deserted to David.
key: As David went to Ziklag, he joined David as a chief of thousands in Manasseh (1 Chronicles 12).
These men helped David against the band of raiders and became commanders in his army (1 Chronicles 12).

name: Jubal
who: A son of Lamech and Adah, the father of all who play the lyre and pipe.
key: Adah bore Jubal to Lamech, a descendant of Cain (Genesis 4).
He was the father of all those who play the lyre and pipe (Genesis 4).

name: Judah
who: Fourth son of Jacob and Leah, ancestor of the tribe of Judah and of King David.
key: He was born to Leah, who named him in praise of the Lord (Genesis 29).
He proposed selling his brother Joseph to traders rather than killing him (Genesis 37).

name: Judah
who: A Levite in Ezra's day who had married a foreign woman after the return from exile.
key: He is listed among the Levites who had married foreign women (Ezra 10).
The assembly agreed with Ezra to put away such marriages and keep the covenant (Ezra 10).

name: Judah
who: A Benjaminite son of Hassenuah who was second in charge over Jerusalem after the exile.
key: When the people resettled Jerusalem, he served as second over the city (Nehemiah 11).
He served with Joel son of Zichri, the overseer of the Benjaminites there (Nehemiah 11).

name: Judah
who: A Levite who returned from exile with Zerubbabel and Jeshua.
key: He is listed among the Levites who came up from Babylon with Zerubbabel (Nehemiah 12).
A Judah also walked with the leaders in the procession dedicating Jerusalem's wall (Nehemiah 12).

name: Judah
who: A Levite musician, a kinsman of Zechariah, at the dedication of Jerusalem's wall.
key: He played the musical instruments of David in the procession dedicating the wall (Nehemiah 12).
Ezra the scribe led his group along the wall toward the Fountain Gate (Nehemiah 12).

name: Judas Iscariot
who: One of the twelve apostles, son of Simon Iscariot, who betrayed Jesus.
key: Jesus chose Judas Iscariot as one of the twelve apostles (Matthew 10; Luke 6).
He kept the disciples' moneybag and stole from it (John 12).

name: Jude
who: A brother of Jesus and of James, who wrote the Letter of Jude.
key: He is named among Jesus' brothers when Nazareth took offense at Jesus (Matthew 13).
During Jesus' ministry his brothers did not yet believe in him (John 7).

name: Julius
who: A Roman centurion of the Augustan Cohort who escorted Paul by sea to Rome.
key: He was given charge of Paul and other prisoners sailing for Italy (Acts 27).
He treated Paul kindly, letting him visit friends at Sidon (Acts 27).

name: Kadmiel
who: Levite family head who returned from exile with Zerubbabel and served in temple rebuilding and worship.
key: Levites of the family of Jeshua and Kadmiel returned from exile with Zerubbabel (Ezra 2).
Kadmiel and his sons helped supervise the workmen rebuilding the temple (Ezra 3).

name: Kareah
who: Father of Johanan and Jonathan, army captains in Judah after the fall of Jerusalem.
key: His son Johanan came to Governor Gedaliah at Mizpah (2 Kings 25).
Johanan and Jonathan, his sons, joined Gedaliah with their men (Jeremiah 40).

name: Kedar
who: Second son of Ishmael, whose descendants became a prominent Arabian tribe known by his name.
key: He was born the second son of Ishmael, one of twelve princes from Ishmael (Genesis 25).
Solomon's song compares the beloved's dark beauty to the tents of Kedar (Song of Solomon 1).

name: Kenaz
who: A grandson of Esau through Eliphaz who became a chief in Edom.
key: He is listed among the sons of Eliphaz, Esau's firstborn (Genesis 36).
He was one of the chiefs descended from Esau in the land of Edom (Genesis 36).

name: Kenaz
who: A chief of Edom named in the later list of Esau's clan chiefs.
key: He is listed among the chiefs of Edom by their clans and dwelling places (Genesis 36).
Chronicles repeats his name among the chiefs of Edom (1 Chronicles 1).

name: Kenaz
who: A man of Judah, father of Othniel, Israel's first judge, and of Seraiah.
key: His son Othniel captured Debir and received Caleb's daughter Achsah as his wife (Joshua 15).
Judges again records Othniel son of Kenaz taking Debir (Judges 1).

name: Kenaz
who: A grandson of Caleb son of Jephunneh, listed in the genealogy of Judah.
key: Chronicles lists him as the son of Elah, son of Caleb son of Jephunneh (1 Chronicles 4).
His father Elah was one of Caleb's three sons, with Iru and Naam (1 Chronicles 4).

name: Keturah
who: A wife of Abraham whose sons were sent east and fathered peoples such as Midian.
key: Abraham took another wife named Keturah (Genesis 25).
She bore him Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah (Genesis 25).

name: Kish
who: A wealthy Benjaminite, son of Abiel, best known as the father of Saul, Israel's first king.
key: He sent his son Saul to search for lost donkeys, a journey that led Saul to Samuel (1 Samuel 9).
When Saul prophesied among the prophets, people asked what had happened to the son of Kish (1 Samuel 10).

name: Kish
who: A Merarite Levite, son of Mahli, whose family served in David's Levite divisions.
key: He is listed with his brother Eleazar as sons of Mahli in David's Levite divisions (1 Chronicles 23).
Eleazar had only daughters, and Kish's sons married them (1 Chronicles 23).

name: Kishi
who: A Merarite Levite, father of Ethan, one of the chief singers David appointed.
key: Ethan son of Kishi, of the sons of Merari, stood at Heman's left among the singers (1 Chronicles 6).
Chronicles later names Ethan's father as Kushaiah (1 Chronicles 15).

name: Kittim
who: A son of Javan in the Table of Nations, ancestor of a seafaring coastland people.
key: He is listed among the sons of Javan, son of Japheth (Genesis 10).
From Javan's sons the coastland peoples spread out in their lands (Genesis 10).

name: Kohath
who: The second son of Levi and grandfather of Moses, Aaron, and Miriam.
key: Kohath went down to Egypt with Levi and Jacob's household (Genesis 46).
He lived 133 years, and his son Amram fathered Aaron and Moses (Exodus 6).

name: Kolaiah
who: A Benjaminite, son of Maaseiah and father of Pedaiah, in the ancestry of Sallu of Jerusalem.
key: Sallu son of Meshullam is traced through Joed, Pedaiah, Kolaiah, Maaseiah, and Ithiel to Jeshaiah (Nehemiah 11).
These Benjaminites were among the people who lived in Jerusalem, the holy city (Nehemiah 11).

name: Kolaiah
who: The father of Ahab, a false prophet among the exiles in Babylon whom Jeremiah condemned.
key: The LORD said Ahab son of Kolaiah was prophesying a lie in his name (Jeremiah 29).
He foretold that Nebuchadnezzar would kill Ahab and Zedekiah before the exiles' eyes (Jeremiah 29).

name: Korah
who: A son of Esau by Oholibamah, born in Canaan, who became a chief in Edom.
key: Oholibamah bore him to Esau in Canaan, with his brothers Jeush and Jalam (Genesis 36).
He became one of the chiefs descended from Esau (Genesis 36).

name: Korah
who: An Edomite chief listed among the descendants of Eliphaz, Esau's firstborn.
key: He is named among the chiefs of the sons of Eliphaz in Edom (Genesis 36).
These chiefs descended from Adah, Esau's wife and Eliphaz's mother (Genesis 36).

name: Korah
who: A Levite, son of Izhar, who led a rebellion against Moses and Aaron.
key: Korah was a grandson of Kohath, son of Levi (Exodus 6).
With Dathan, Abiram, and 250 leaders, he challenged Moses and Aaron (Numbers 16).

name: Kore
who: A Korahite Levite, son of Ebiasaph, whose sons led the temple gatekeepers.
key: His son Shallum and their kinsmen guarded the thresholds of the tent, as their fathers had (1 Chronicles 9).
His son Meshelemiah headed a family of gatekeepers in David's time (1 Chronicles 26).

name: Ladan
who: Levite son of Gershon whose descendants served in the tabernacle and temple.
key: As Libni, he is listed among the sons of Gershon, son of Levi (Exodus 6).
The Libnites were a Gershonite clan who served at the tabernacle (Numbers 3).

name: Laban
who: Rebekah's brother in Haran, father of Leah and Rachel, and Jacob's uncle and father-in-law.
key: He welcomed Abraham's servant and agreed to Rebekah's marriage to Isaac (Genesis 24).
He gave Leah to Jacob in place of Rachel, then gave Rachel for seven more years (Genesis 29).

name: Lahmi
who: A Philistine warrior, brother of Goliath, killed by Elhanan in David's wars.
key: In renewed war with the Philistines, Elhanan son of Jair struck him down (1 Chronicles 20).
He was among the descendants of the giants in Gath who fell to David's men (1 Chronicles 20).

name: Laish
who: A man of Gallim, father of Palti, to whom Saul gave David's wife Michal.
key: Saul gave Michal, David's wife, to his son Palti of Gallim (1 Samuel 25).
Later Ish-bosheth took Michal from his son and returned her to David (2 Samuel 3).

name: Lamech
who: A descendant of Cain who took two wives and boasted of avenging himself.
key: He took two wives, Adah and Zillah (Genesis 4).
His sons Jabal, Jubal, and Tubal-cain began herding, music, and metalworking (Genesis 4).

name: Lamech
who: A son of Methuselah and the father of Noah in the line from Adam.
key: He fathered a son at 182 and named him Noah (Genesis 5).
He hoped Noah would bring relief from the painful toil of the cursed ground (Genesis 5).

name: Lapidoth
who: The husband of Deborah, the prophetess who judged Israel.
key: Deborah is introduced as a prophetess and the wife of Lapidoth (Judges 4).
In those days Deborah judged Israel and summoned Barak to fight Sisera (Judges 4).

name: Lazarus
who: The poor beggar in Jesus' story of the rich man and Lazarus.
key: He lay covered with sores at a rich man's gate, longing for scraps (Luke 16).
When he died, angels carried him to Abraham's side, while the rich man suffered (Luke 16).

name: Lazarus
who: A man of Bethany, brother of Martha and Mary, whom Jesus loved and raised from the dead.
key: He fell ill and died, and Jesus came to Bethany after he had been in the tomb four days (John 11).
Jesus wept, then called him out of the tomb alive (John 11).

name: Leah
who: Laban's elder daughter, Jacob's first wife, and mother of six of his sons.
key: Laban gave Leah to Jacob in place of Rachel on the wedding night (Genesis 29).
The Lord saw she was unloved and gave her Reuben, Simeon, Levi, and Judah (Genesis 29).

name: Thaddaeus
who: One of the twelve apostles, called Thaddaeus in Matthew and Mark and Judas son of James in Luke and Acts.
key: Jesus named Thaddaeus among the twelve apostles he sent out (Matthew 10).
Luke lists this apostle as Judas son of James, distinct from Judas Iscariot (Luke 6).

name: Lemuel
who: A king whose mother's teaching is recorded in the final chapter of Proverbs.
key: Proverbs records the words his mother taught him as king (Proverbs 31).
She warned him against women and wine and urged him to defend the poor and needy (Proverbs 31).

name: Letushim
label: People group
who: An Arabian people descended from Dedan, a grandson of Abraham and Keturah.
key: The sons of Dedan were Asshurim, Letushim, and Leummim (Genesis 25).
Abraham gave gifts to his sons by his concubines and sent them east, away from Isaac (Genesis 25).

name: Levi
who: Third son of Jacob and Leah, ancestor of the Levites, Israel's priestly tribe.
key: He was born to Leah, who hoped her husband would now be attached to her (Genesis 29).
With Simeon, he killed the men of Shechem to avenge their sister Dinah (Genesis 34).

name: Lo-ammi
who: The third child of Gomer, Hosea's wife, whose name announced judgment on Israel.
key: Gomer bore him after weaning her daughter Lo-ruhamah (Hosea 1).
God named him to declare that Israel was not his people (Hosea 1).

name: Lo-ruhamah
who: The daughter of Gomer, Hosea's wife, whose name announced God's withdrawn mercy from Israel.
key: Gomer bore a daughter after her son Jezreel (Hosea 1).
God named her to show he would no longer have mercy on Israel (Hosea 1).

name: Lois
who: The grandmother of Timothy, whose sincere faith Paul remembered.
key: Paul recalled the sincere faith that dwelt first in Timothy's grandmother Lois (2 Timothy 1).
That same faith lived in Timothy's mother Eunice and in Timothy himself (2 Timothy 1).

name: Lot
who: Abraham's nephew, son of Haran, who settled near Sodom and was rescued from its destruction.
key: Lot traveled with his uncle Abram from Haran to Canaan (Genesis 12).
When their herds grew too large, Lot chose the Jordan valley near Sodom (Genesis 13).

name: Lotan
who: A son of Seir the Horite and one of the Horite chiefs in the land of Seir.
key: Lotan is listed among the sons of Seir the Horite, the inhabitants of the land (Genesis 36).
His sons were Hori and Hemam, and his sister was Timna (Genesis 36).

name: Lucius
who: A prophet and teacher from Cyrene in the church at Antioch.
key: He was among the prophets and teachers at Antioch when the Spirit set apart Barnabas and Saul (Acts 13).
A Lucius, called Paul's kinsman, sent greetings to the church in Rome (Romans 16).

name: Luke
who: A beloved physician and companion of Paul, traditionally recognized as the author of Luke and Acts.
key: The Gospel traditionally ascribed to Luke opens as an orderly account for Theophilus (Luke 1).
Paul sent greetings from Luke the beloved physician to the Colossians (Colossians 4).

name: Lydia
who: A seller of purple goods from Thyatira, the first recorded believer in Philippi through Paul.
key: A worshiper of God, she heard Paul speak by the riverside at Philippi (Acts 16).
The Lord opened her heart, and she and her household were baptized (Acts 16).

name: Maacah
who: A wife of David, daughter of King Talmai of Geshur, and mother of Absalom.
key: She bore Absalom, David's third son, at Hebron (2 Samuel 3).
After killing Amnon, Absalom fled to her father Talmai in Geshur for three years (2 Samuel 13).

name: Maacah
who: A child of Nahor, Abraham's brother, by his concubine Reumah.
key: Abraham was told that Nahor's concubine Reumah bore Tebah, Gaham, Tahash, and Maacah (Genesis 22).
This news of Nahor's family came after God provided a ram in place of Isaac (Genesis 22).

name: Maacah
who: Favored wife of King Rehoboam and mother of King Abijah, later removed as queen mother for idolatry.
key: Rehoboam loved her above his other wives and made her son Abijah chief prince (2 Chronicles 11).
Her son Abijah reigned three years over Judah (1 Kings 15).

name: Maacah
who: A concubine of Caleb son of Hezron, and mother of sons who fathered towns in Judah.
key: Maacah, Caleb's concubine, bore Sheber and Tirhanah (1 Chronicles 2).
She also bore Shaaph the father of Madmannah, and Sheva the father of Machbenah and Gibea (1 Chronicles 2).

name: Maaseiah
who: A Benjaminite, son of Ithiel and father of Kolaiah, in the ancestry of Sallu of Jerusalem.
key: Sallu son of Meshullam is traced through Joed, Pedaiah, Kolaiah, Maaseiah, and Ithiel to Jeshaiah (Nehemiah 11).
These Benjaminites were among the people who lived in Jerusalem, the holy city (Nehemiah 11).

name: Maaseiah
who: Father of Zephaniah, a leading priest in Jerusalem during King Zedekiah's reign.
key: His son Zephaniah was sent by Zedekiah to ask Jeremiah to inquire of the LORD (Jeremiah 21).
Shemaiah wrote from Babylon urging his son Zephaniah to restrain Jeremiah (Jeremiah 29).

name: Maaseiah
who: Father of Zedekiah, a false prophet among the exiles in Babylon.
key: His son Zedekiah prophesied lies in the LORD's name among the exiles (Jeremiah 29).
Jeremiah foretold that the king of Babylon would roast Zedekiah and Ahab in the fire (Jeremiah 29).

name: Maaz
who: A man of Judah, son of Ram, the firstborn of Jerahmeel, named in Chronicles' genealogy of Judah.
key: Maaz was a son of Ram, the firstborn of Jerahmeel (1 Chronicles 2).
His brothers were Jamin and Eker (1 Chronicles 2).

name: Machir
who: Son of Manasseh and grandson of Joseph, ancestor of the Machirite clan and father of Gilead.
key: His children were born on Joseph's knees (Genesis 50).
He was the father of Gilead and head of the Machirite clan (Numbers 26).

name: Machir
who: A man of Lo-debar who sheltered Mephibosheth and later supplied David in exile.
key: Mephibosheth was living in his house at Lo-debar when David sent for him (2 Samuel 9).
He brought beds, food, and supplies to David at Mahanaim during Absalom's revolt (2 Samuel 17).

name: Magog
who: A son of Japheth in the table of nations, whose name later designates a distant northern land and people.
key: Magog is listed among the sons of Japheth, son of Noah (Genesis 10).
Chronicles repeats his name among Japheth's descendants (1 Chronicles 1).

name: Mahalalel
who: A son of Kenan and father of Jared in the line from Adam to Noah.
key: He was born when his father Kenan was seventy (Genesis 5).
He fathered Jared at sixty-five and lived 895 years (Genesis 5).

name: Mahalath
who: A granddaughter of David through his son Jerimoth who became a wife of King Rehoboam.
key: Rehoboam took as wife Mahalath, the daughter of Jerimoth son of David (2 Chronicles 11).
Abihail, daughter of Eliab son of Jesse, is also named in her family line (2 Chronicles 11).

name: Maharai
who: A Netophathite of the Zerahite clan, one of David's mighty men and a division commander.
key: He is listed among David's thirty mighty men (2 Samuel 23).
He commanded the army division of 24,000 that served in the tenth month (1 Chronicles 27).

name: Maher-shalal-hash-baz
who: A son of Isaiah whose name was a sign of Assyria's coming plunder of Damascus and Samaria.
key: God told Isaiah to write the name on a large tablet before reliable witnesses (Isaiah 8).
The prophetess bore a son, and the LORD told Isaiah to give him this name (Isaiah 8).

name: Mahli
who: Levite son of Merari, ancestor of the Mahlite clan that served at the tabernacle and temple.
key: He is listed as a son of Merari, son of Levi (Exodus 6).
The Mahlites were one of the Merarite clans serving at the tabernacle (Numbers 3).

name: Mahli
who: A Merarite Levite, son of Mushi, whose family served in David's Levite divisions.
key: He appears in the ancestry of Ethan, a Levite singer appointed in David's time (1 Chronicles 6).
He is listed with Eder and Jeremoth as sons of Mushi in David's Levite divisions (1 Chronicles 23).

name: Mahol
who: Father of the wise men Heman, Calcol, and Darda, whose wisdom Solomon surpassed.
key: Solomon was wiser than Heman, Calcol, and Darda, the sons of Mahol (1 Kings 4).
Solomon's wisdom surpassed the wisdom of all the people of the east and of Egypt (1 Kings 4).

name: Malachi
who: The prophet whose book of the LORD's word to Israel closes the Old Testament.
key: His book opens as the oracle of the LORD's word to Israel by Malachi (Malachi 1).
He rebuked the priests for offering blemished animals on the LORD's altar (Malachi 1).

name: Malchi-shua
who: A son of King Saul who died with his father and brothers on Mount Gilboa.
key: He is named with Jonathan and Ishvi among the sons of Saul (1 Samuel 14).
The Philistines killed him with Jonathan and Abinadab on Mount Gilboa (1 Samuel 31).

name: Malchiel
who: A grandson of Asher who went down to Egypt with Jacob's family.
key: He went down to Egypt with Jacob as a son of Beriah, son of Asher (Genesis 46).
He became the ancestor of the Malchielite clan in the tribe of Asher (Numbers 26).

name: Malchijah
who: A priest named in the ancestry of Adaiah, a priest who served in Jerusalem after the exile.
key: Adaiah's line is traced through Jeroham and Pashhur back to Malchijah (1 Chronicles 9).
Nehemiah also records this priestly line among those living in Jerusalem (Nehemiah 11).

name: Malchijah
who: A returned exile named in Ezra's list of men who had married foreign women.
key: He is listed among the Israelites who had married foreign women (Ezra 10).
The assembly agreed with Ezra to put away such marriages (Ezra 10).

name: Malchijah
who: A son of Harim who helped rebuild Jerusalem's wall under Nehemiah.
key: He and Hasshub repaired a section of the wall and the Tower of the Ovens (Nehemiah 3).
The wall was finished in fifty-two days despite fierce opposition (Nehemiah 6).

name: Mamre
who: An Amorite near Hebron, brother of Eshcol and Aner, and an ally of Abram.
key: Abram lived by the oaks of Mamre the Amorite, who was allied with him (Genesis 14).
After Abram rescued Lot, he asked that Mamre receive his share of the spoil (Genesis 14).

name: Manahath
who: A Horite descendant of Seir, son of Shobal, living in the land later called Edom.
key: He is listed among the sons of Shobal, son of Seir the Horite (Genesis 36).
Chronicles repeats him among the descendants of Seir (1 Chronicles 1).

name: Manasseh
who: Firstborn son of Joseph born in Egypt, ancestor of the tribe of Manasseh.
key: Joseph named him Manasseh because God had made him forget his hardship (Genesis 41).
Jacob blessed him but placed his younger brother Ephraim ahead of him (Genesis 48).

name: Manasseh
who: A king of Judah, son of Hezekiah, whose long reign was marked by idolatry until he repented.
key: Manasseh became king at twelve and reigned fifty-five years (2 Kings 21).
He rebuilt high places, set idols in the temple, and burned his son (2 Kings 21).

name: Manoah
who: Danite from Zorah and father of Samson.
key: The angel of the LORD told his barren wife she would bear a son (Judges 13).
He prayed that the man of God would return to teach them (Judges 13).

name: Mark
who: Early Christian worker, cousin of Barnabas, who served alongside Paul, Barnabas, and Peter.
key: After his release from prison, Peter went to the house of Mary, mother of John Mark (Acts 12).
He assisted Barnabas and Saul in Cyprus but left them at Perga and returned to Jerusalem (Acts 13).

name: Martha
who: A woman of Bethany, sister of Mary and Lazarus, who welcomed Jesus into her home.
key: She welcomed Jesus, became anxious with serving, and was told Mary had chosen the good portion (Luke 10).
When Lazarus died, she met Jesus and confessed him as the Christ, the Son of God (John 11).

name: Mary
who: The virgin from Nazareth, betrothed to Joseph, who gave birth to Jesus the Messiah.
key: The angel Gabriel told her she would conceive by the Holy Spirit and bear Jesus (Luke 1).
She visited Elizabeth and praised God in a song of thanksgiving (Luke 1).

name: Mary of Bethany
who: A woman of Bethany, sister of Martha and Lazarus, who sat at Jesus' feet and later anointed him.
key: She sat at the Lord's feet listening, and Jesus said she had chosen the good portion (Luke 10).
After Lazarus died, she fell at Jesus' feet weeping, and Jesus was deeply moved (John 11).

name: Mary the mother of James
who: Follower of Jesus, mother of James the younger and Joses, who witnessed his crucifixion, burial, and empty tomb.
key: She watched Jesus' crucifixion from a distance with other women from Galilee (Matthew 27).
She saw where Jesus' body was laid in the tomb (Mark 15).

name: Mary
who: The mother of John Mark, whose house in Jerusalem was a gathering place for the church.
key: Many believers gathered at her house to pray while Peter was in prison (Acts 12).
Freed by an angel, Peter went to her house, where Rhoda answered his knock (Acts 12).

name: Mary Magdalene
who: Follower of Jesus, freed from seven demons, who first saw the risen Lord.
key: Jesus cast seven demons from her, and she supported his ministry (Luke 8).
She stood near the cross with Jesus' mother (John 19).

name: Matthan
who: Son of Eleazar and grandfather of Joseph, Mary's husband, in Matthew's genealogy of Jesus.
key: Matthew lists Matthan son of Eleazar in Jesus' royal line descended from David (Matthew 1).
Matthan fathered Jacob, the father of Joseph the husband of Mary (Matthew 1).

name: Matthew
who: Tax collector, also called Levi, whom Jesus called to follow him and appointed one of the twelve apostles.
key: Jesus saw him at the tax booth and said to follow him, and he did (Matthew 9).
He held a great feast where Jesus ate with tax collectors and sinners (Luke 5).

name: Matthias
who: The disciple chosen by lot to replace Judas Iscariot among the twelve apostles.
key: He had followed Jesus from John's baptism until the ascension (Acts 1).
He and Joseph called Barsabbas were put forward, and the apostles prayed (Acts 1).

name: Mattithiah
who: A Korahite Levite, firstborn of Shallum, in charge of baking the flat cakes.
key: As Shallum's firstborn, he was trusted with making the flat cakes for the temple (1 Chronicles 9).
He served among the Levites who lived in Jerusalem after the return from exile (1 Chronicles 9).

name: Mattithiah
who: A Levite musician, son of Jeduthun, who played the lyre in worship before the ark under David.
key: Mattithiah was appointed among the Levites to play lyres when the ark was brought up (1 Chronicles 15).
He served under Asaph with harps and lyres before the ark of the Lord (1 Chronicles 16).

name: Medad
who: One of Israel's seventy elders who prophesied in the camp when the Spirit rested on him in the wilderness.
key: Medad was registered among the seventy elders but remained in the camp instead of going to the tent (Numbers 11).
The Spirit rested on Medad and Eldad, and they prophesied in the camp (Numbers 11).

name: Medan
who: A son of Abraham by Keturah, sent away eastward with his brothers.
key: Keturah bore Abraham Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah (Genesis 25).
Abraham gave gifts to his concubines' sons and sent them east, away from Isaac (Genesis 25).

name: Mehetabel
who: Named in Nehemiah as the parent of Delaiah, whose son Shemaiah was hired to frighten Nehemiah.
key: Nehemiah went to the house of Shemaiah son of Delaiah, son of Mehetabel (Nehemiah 6).
Nehemiah perceived that Tobiah and Sanballat had hired Shemaiah against him (Nehemiah 6).

name: Mehujael
who: A descendant of Cain, son of Irad and father of Methushael, in the line leading to Lamech.
key: Irad fathered Mehujael, and Mehujael fathered Methushael (Genesis 4).
Methushael fathered Lamech, who took two wives, Adah and Zillah (Genesis 4).

name: Malchiah
who: Father of Pashhur, an official of King Zedekiah who sought Jeremiah's death.
key: King Zedekiah sent Pashhur son of Malchiah to Jeremiah to inquire of the LORD (Jeremiah 21).
Pashhur son of Malchiah was among the officials who heard Jeremiah and urged that he be put to death (Jeremiah 38).

name: Melchizedek
who: The king of Salem and priest of God Most High who blessed Abram, a type of Christ's priesthood.
key: He brought out bread and wine, blessed Abram, and received a tenth of everything (Genesis 14).
The psalmist declared the Lord's king a priest forever after his order (Psalm 110).

name: Melech
who: A son of Micah and great-grandson of Jonathan, listed in the genealogy of King Saul's family.
key: Melech is listed as a son of Micah, son of Merib-baal, in Saul's line through Jonathan (1 Chronicles 8).
The genealogy of Saul's descendants is repeated, again naming Melech among Micah's sons (1 Chronicles 9).

name: Menahem
who: Son of Gadi who seized Israel's throne by killing Shallum and paid tribute to Assyria.
key: He struck down Shallum in Samaria and reigned in his place (2 Kings 15).
He attacked Tiphsah brutally because it would not open its gates to him (2 Kings 15).

name: Meonothai
who: A son of Othniel, Israel's first judge, listed in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah.
key: Meonothai is named with his brother Hathath as a son of Othniel (1 Chronicles 4).
He fathered Ophrah, continuing Othniel's family line in Judah (1 Chronicles 4).

name: Mephibosheth
who: Son of Jonathan and grandson of Saul, lame in both feet, shown kindness by David.
key: He became lame at five when his nurse fell while fleeing (2 Samuel 4).
David restored Saul's land to him and he ate at the king's table (2 Samuel 9).

name: Meraiah
who: A priest who headed the priestly family of Seraiah in the days of the high priest Joiakim.
key: In the days of Joiakim, Meraiah was head of the priestly father's house of Seraiah (Nehemiah 12).
He is listed first among the priestly family heads of that generation (Nehemiah 12).

name: Meraioth
who: A priest descended from Aaron through Eleazar, listed in the line of the high priests.
key: He was the son of Zerahiah and father of Amariah in Aaron's line (1 Chronicles 6).
His name appears in the priestly ancestry of Ezra the scribe (Ezra 7).

name: Merari
who: The third son of Levi, whose descendants the Merarites served at the tabernacle.
key: Merari went down to Egypt with his father Levi and Jacob's household (Genesis 46).
The Merarites were assigned to carry the tabernacle frames, bars, and pillars (Numbers 3; Numbers 4).

name: Meremoth
who: A priest, son of Uriah, who served in Jerusalem in the days of Ezra and Nehemiah.
key: He received and weighed the silver and gold brought to the temple by Ezra's group (Ezra 8).
He repaired two sections of Jerusalem's wall, one beside Eliashib's house (Nehemiah 3).

name: Merodach-baladan
who: A king of Babylon, son of Baladan, who sent envoys to King Hezekiah after Hezekiah recovered from illness.
key: Hearing of Hezekiah's illness and recovery, he sent envoys with letters and a gift (Isaiah 39).
Hezekiah welcomed the envoys and showed them all the treasures in his storehouses (Isaiah 39).

name: Mesha
who: A king of Moab, a sheep breeder who paid tribute to Israel and rebelled after Ahab's death.
key: Mesha paid Israel's king a heavy yearly tribute of lambs and wool (2 Kings 3).
After Ahab died, Mesha rebelled, and the kings of Israel, Judah, and Edom marched against him (2 Kings 3).

name: Meshach
who: One of Daniel's three Judean friends in Babylon, kept safe by God in the fiery furnace.
key: Taken to Babylon, he was renamed Meshach and avoided the king's food (Daniel 1).
He prayed with Daniel for God to reveal the king's dream (Daniel 2).

name: Meshech
who: A son of Japheth and grandson of Noah, whose descendants became a distant northern people.
key: He is listed among the sons of Japheth in the table of nations (Genesis 10).
Meshech traded slaves and bronze vessels with the city of Tyre (Ezekiel 27).

name: Meshelemiah
who: A Korahite Levite, son of Kore, who headed a family of gatekeepers in David's time.
key: His son Zechariah was gatekeeper at the entrance of the tent of meeting (1 Chronicles 9).
Meshelemiah son of Kore was a Korahite gatekeeper with seven sons (1 Chronicles 26).

name: Meshillemith
who: A priest of the family of Immer, named in the ancestry of priests serving in Jerusalem after the exile.
key: Meshillemith appears in the ancestry of the priest Maasai, as son of Immer and father of Meshullam (1 Chronicles 9).
Nehemiah's parallel list calls him Meshillemoth, an ancestor of the priest Amashsai (Nehemiah 11).

name: Meshullam
who: A Gadite, one of the seven sons of Abihail who headed fathers' houses in Gilead and Bashan.
key: Abihail's sons Michael, Meshullam, Sheba, Jorai, Jacan, Zia, and Eber headed their fathers' houses (1 Chronicles 5).
These Gadites lived in Gilead, in Bashan and its towns, and in the pasturelands of Sharon (1 Chronicles 5).

name: Meshullam
who: A Benjaminite, son of Hodaviah, whose son Sallu lived in Jerusalem after the return from exile.
key: Meshullam is listed as son of Hodaviah in the genealogy of the Benjaminites (1 Chronicles 9).
His son Sallu was among the Benjaminites who settled in Jerusalem after the exile (1 Chronicles 9).

name: Meshullam
who: A Benjaminite, son of Shephatiah, who was a head of a father's house living in Jerusalem after the exile.
key: Meshullam son of Shephatiah is listed among the Benjaminites living in Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 9).
He was counted among the heads of fathers' houses in their families (1 Chronicles 9).

name: Meshullam
who: A priest of the house of Immer, son of Meshillemith, named in the ancestry of a priest serving in Jerusalem.
key: Meshullam son of Meshillemith appears in the ancestry of the priest Maasai, of the house of Immer (1 Chronicles 9).
His descendants were among the priests who lived in Jerusalem after the exile (1 Chronicles 9).

name: Meshullam
who: A Benjaminite, son of Joed, whose son Sallu settled in Jerusalem in Nehemiah's day.
key: Meshullam is listed as son of Joed in the line of the Benjaminites (Nehemiah 11).
His son Sallu was among the leaders of Benjamin who lived in Jerusalem (Nehemiah 11).

name: Methuselah
who: A son of Enoch and grandfather of Noah, the longest-lived person recorded in Scripture.
key: He was born when his father Enoch was sixty-five (Genesis 5).
He fathered Lamech at 187 and lived 969 years in all (Genesis 5).

name: Micah
who: Man of the hill country of Ephraim who set up a household shrine with idols in the time of the judges.
key: He returned stolen silver to his mother, who had an idol made from it (Judges 17).
He made a shrine with an ephod and household gods and installed his son as priest (Judges 17).

name: Micah
who: A Reubenite in the line of Joel, son of Shimei and father of Reaiah.
key: The sons of Joel are traced through Shemaiah, Gog, Shimei, Micah, Reaiah, and Baal (1 Chronicles 5).
The line continued to Beerah, a Reubenite chief whom Tiglath-pileser of Assyria carried into exile (1 Chronicles 5).

name: Micah
who: A prophet from Moresheth who warned Samaria and Jerusalem of judgment and foretold a ruler from Bethlehem.
key: Micah prophesied in the days of Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, concerning Samaria and Jerusalem (Micah 1).
He warned that because of corrupt leaders, Zion would be plowed as a field (Micah 3).

name: Micah
who: Son of Mephibosheth and great-grandson of Saul, through whom Saul's family line continued.
key: Mephibosheth, whom David cared for, had a young son named Mica (2 Samuel 9).
As son of Merib-baal, he fathered Pithon, Melech, Tarea, and Ahaz (1 Chronicles 8).

name: Micaiah
who: Prophet of the LORD, son of Imlah, who foretold King Ahab's defeat and death in battle.
key: Ahab hated him because he never prophesied good concerning him (1 Kings 22).
He saw Israel scattered on the mountains like sheep without a shepherd (1 Kings 22).

name: Michael
who: A man of the tribe of Gad, son of Jeshishai, listed in the Gadite genealogy.
key: He appears in the ancestry of Abihail's family as son of Jeshishai and father of Gilead (1 Chronicles 5).
These Gadites were recorded in genealogies in the days of Jotham of Judah and Jeroboam of Israel (1 Chronicles 5).

name: Michael
who: A Benjaminite, son of Beriah, named among the family heads of Benjamin who lived in Jerusalem.
key: Michael, Ispah, and Joha are named among the sons of Beriah (1 Chronicles 8).
Beriah and Shema, heads in Aijalon, had put the inhabitants of Gath to flight (1 Chronicles 8).

name: Michael
who: An archangel, described as a chief prince who stands guard over God's people.
key: Michael, one of the chief princes, came to help against the prince of Persia (Daniel 10).
He is called the great prince who protects Daniel's people in a time of trouble (Daniel 12).

name: Michal
who: Younger daughter of King Saul and the first wife of David.
key: She loved David, and Saul gave her to him as wife (1 Samuel 18).
She helped David escape through a window and deceived Saul's messengers (1 Samuel 19).

name: Midian
who: A son of Abraham by Keturah and ancestor of the Midianites.
key: Keturah bore Midian and his brothers to Abraham (Genesis 25).
Abraham gave gifts to Keturah's sons and sent them east, away from Isaac (Genesis 25).

name: Milcah
who: A daughter of Haran, wife of Abraham's brother Nahor, and grandmother of Rebekah.
key: She was the daughter of Haran and married Nahor, Abraham's brother (Genesis 11).
She bore eight sons to Nahor, including Bethuel, father of Rebekah (Genesis 22).

name: Milcom
label: False god
who: The detestable god of the Ammonites, whose worship Solomon brought into Israel and Josiah later abolished.
key: In his old age Solomon went after Milcom, the abomination of the Ammonites (1 Kings 11).
God tore ten tribes from Solomon's house because they had worshiped Milcom and other gods (1 Kings 11).

name: Miriam
who: A prophetess, sister of Moses and Aaron, who led Israel's women in praise after the Red Sea crossing.
key: She took a tambourine and led the women in singing to the Lord after the Red Sea crossing (Exodus 15).
She and Aaron spoke against Moses, and she was struck with leprosy for seven days (Numbers 12).

name: Mishael
who: A Levite of the clan of Kohath, son of Uzziel and cousin of Moses and Aaron.
key: Mishael is listed as a son of Uzziel, son of Kohath, with Elzaphan and Sithri (Exodus 6).
After Nadab and Abihu died, Moses had Mishael and Elzaphan carry their bodies out of the camp (Leviticus 10).

name: Mizzah
who: A grandson of Esau through his son Reuel, and a chief among the Edomites.
key: Mizzah was a son of Reuel, Esau's son by Basemath (Genesis 36).
He is named among the chiefs of the sons of Reuel in Edom (Genesis 36).

name: Moab
who: Son of Lot by his older daughter and ancestor of the Moabites, the nation east of the Dead Sea.
key: He was born to Lot's older daughter after she made her father drunk in a cave (Genesis 19).
His descendants, the Moabites, became a nation that often opposed Israel (Numbers 22).

name: Molech
label: False god
who: A god of the Ammonites associated with child sacrifice, whose worship the LORD forbade.
key: The law forbade Israel to give any of their children to Molech (Leviticus 18).
Anyone who gave a child to Molech was to be put to death (Leviticus 20).

name: Molid
who: A man of Judah in Jerahmeel's line, son of Abishur and his wife Abihail.
key: Abishur's wife Abihail bore him Ahban and Molid (1 Chronicles 2).
He is listed among the descendants of Jerahmeel, son of Hezron (1 Chronicles 2).

name: Mordecai
who: Jewish exile of the tribe of Benjamin in Susa who raised his cousin Esther and helped save his people.
key: He raised his orphaned cousin Esther and uncovered a plot against King Ahasuerus (Esther 2).
He refused to bow to Haman, who then plotted to destroy all the Jews (Esther 3).

name: Moses
who: Hebrew prophet and lawgiver whom God used to lead Israel out of Egypt and give the law at Sinai.
key: As a baby he was hidden in a basket and adopted by Pharaoh's daughter (Exodus 2).
God called him from a burning bush to deliver Israel from Egypt (Exodus 3).

name: Moza
who: A man of Judah, son of Caleb by his concubine Ephah, named in Judah's genealogy.
key: Ephah, Caleb's concubine, bore Haran, Moza, and Gazez (1 Chronicles 2).
His father Caleb was the brother of Jerahmeel, both sons of Hezron (1 Chronicles 2).

name: Mushi
who: Levite son of Merari, ancestor of the Mushite clan that served at the tabernacle and temple.
key: He is listed as a son of Merari, son of Levi (Exodus 6).
The Mushites were one of the Merarite clans serving at the tabernacle (Numbers 3).

name: Naam
who: A son of Caleb son of Jephunneh, listed in the genealogy of Judah.
key: Naam is named with Iru and Elah as the sons of Caleb son of Jephunneh (1 Chronicles 4).
His brother Elah was the father of Kenaz (1 Chronicles 4).

name: Naamah
who: Daughter of Lamech and Zillah in Cain's line, and sister of Tubal-cain.
key: Lamech took two wives, Adah and Zillah (Genesis 4).
Zillah bore Tubal-cain, and the sister of Tubal-cain was Naamah (Genesis 4).

name: Naaman
who: A commander of the army of Syria who was healed of leprosy after obeying the prophet Elisha.
key: An Israelite servant girl told his wife that the prophet in Samaria could heal him (2 Kings 5).
Angered at first, he washed seven times in the Jordan and was made clean (2 Kings 5).

name: Nabal
who: Wealthy but harsh Calebite of Maon, the first husband of Abigail.
key: He insulted David's men and refused them provisions at sheep-shearing time (1 Samuel 25).
His wife Abigail brought food to David without telling him (1 Samuel 25).

name: Naboth
who: Man of Jezreel who was killed through Jezebel's plot after refusing to sell his vineyard to Ahab.
key: He refused to give King Ahab his family inheritance (1 Kings 21).
Jezebel arranged false witnesses, and he was stoned to death (1 Kings 21).

name: Nadab
who: The firstborn son of Aaron, ordained as a priest, who died for offering unauthorized fire before the Lord.
key: He went up Mount Sinai with Moses and the elders and saw the God of Israel (Exodus 24).
He was set apart with his brothers to serve the Lord as a priest (Exodus 28).

name: Nadab
who: A son of Jeroboam who reigned over Israel for two years before Baasha assassinated him.
key: Nadab succeeded his father Jeroboam as king of Israel (1 Kings 14).
He reigned two years and did evil, walking in his father's sin (1 Kings 15).

name: Nadab
who: A man of Judah in Jerahmeel's line, son of Shammai and father of Seled and Appaim.
key: The sons of Shammai were Nadab and Abishur (1 Chronicles 2).
The sons of Nadab were Seled and Appaim; Seled died childless (1 Chronicles 2).

name: Naharai
who: A man of Beeroth who served as armor-bearer to Joab and was listed among David's mighty men.
key: Naharai of Beeroth, Joab's armor-bearer, is named among David's thirty mighty men (2 Samuel 23).
The parallel list of David's mighty men again names him as Joab's armor-bearer (1 Chronicles 11).

name: Nahash
who: A king of the Ammonites whose siege of Jabesh-gilead led to Saul's first victory as king.
key: Nahash besieged Jabesh-gilead and demanded to gouge out every man's right eye as terms (1 Samuel 11).
The Spirit of God rushed on Saul, who rallied Israel and defeated the Ammonites (1 Samuel 11).

name: Nahash
who: A king of the Ammonites who showed kindness to David and was succeeded by his son Hanun.
key: Nahash had dealt kindly with David, so David sent servants to console Hanun when Nahash died (2 Samuel 10).
Hanun shamed David's envoys, leading to war between Ammon and Israel (2 Samuel 10).

name: Nahash
who: An Ammonite of Rabbah, father of Shobi, probably the Ammonite king who had shown David kindness.
key: His son Shobi came from Rabbah of the Ammonites to meet David at Mahanaim (2 Samuel 17).
Shobi brought beds, bowls, and food for David's people during Absalom's revolt (2 Samuel 17).

name: Nahath
who: A grandson of Esau through his son Reuel, and a chief among the Edomites.
key: Nahath was a son of Reuel, Esau's son by Basemath (Genesis 36).
He is named among the chiefs of the sons of Reuel in Edom (Genesis 36).

name: Nahor
who: A son of Serug and the father of Terah, making him Abraham's grandfather.
key: He was born when his father Serug was thirty (Genesis 11).
He fathered Terah at twenty-nine and lived 148 years in all (Genesis 11).

name: Nahor
who: Brother of Abraham who settled in Mesopotamia; grandfather of Rebekah and Laban.
key: He married Milcah, the daughter of his brother Haran (Genesis 11).
Abraham heard that Milcah and the concubine Reumah had borne Nahor many children (Genesis 22).

name: Nahshon
who: The son of Amminadab and leader of the tribe of Judah in the wilderness, an ancestor of David and Jesus.
key: His sister Elisheba married Aaron (Exodus 6).
He was appointed chief of the tribe of Judah to help Moses take the census (Numbers 1).

name: Nahum
who: A prophet from Elkosh whose book announces the LORD's judgment on Nineveh, the Assyrian capital.
key: Nahum of Elkosh received a vision concerning Nineveh (Nahum 1).
He proclaimed the LORD slow to anger yet sure to punish the guilty (Nahum 1).

name: Naomi
who: Woman of Bethlehem, mother-in-law of Ruth, who returned home from Moab after losing her family.
key: During a famine she moved to Moab, where her husband and both sons died (Ruth 1).
She returned to Bethlehem with Ruth and asked to be called Mara (Ruth 1).

name: Naphtali
who: Son of Jacob by Rachel's servant Bilhah, ancestor of the tribe of Naphtali in Galilee.
key: Rachel named him Naphtali after her struggles with her sister (Genesis 30).
Jacob blessed him as a doe let loose (Genesis 49).

name: Nathan
who: A son of David and Bathsheba, born in Jerusalem, through whom Luke traces Jesus' genealogy.
key: Nathan was one of the sons born to David in Jerusalem (2 Samuel 5).
Chronicles names him among four sons Bathsheba bore to David, including Solomon (1 Chronicles 3).

name: Nathan
who: A prophet in David's court who delivered God's covenant promise and confronted David's sin.
key: Nathan told David that God would build him a lasting house and kingdom (2 Samuel 7).
He rebuked David's sin with Bathsheba through a parable about a lamb (2 Samuel 12).

name: Nathan
who: A man of Zobah whose son Igal and brother Joel are named among David's mighty men.
key: Igal son of Nathan of Zobah is listed among David's thirty mighty men (2 Samuel 23).
The parallel list names Joel the brother of Nathan among David's mighty men (1 Chronicles 11).

name: Nathanael
who: A disciple from Cana in Galilee whom Philip brought to Jesus.
key: Philip told him they had found the one Moses wrote about, Jesus of Nazareth (John 1).
He doubted that anything good could come from Nazareth (John 1).

name: Neariah
who: A descendant of David's royal line after the exile, son of Shemaiah and father of Hizkiah.
key: Neariah is listed with Hattush, Igal, Bariah, and Shaphat as sons of Shemaiah (1 Chronicles 3).
His sons were Elioenai, Hizkiah, and Azrikam (1 Chronicles 3).

name: Nebaioth
who: The firstborn son of Ishmael, whose descendants became one of the twelve Ishmaelite tribes.
key: Nebaioth was the firstborn of Ishmael's twelve sons, each a tribal prince (Genesis 25).
Esau married Mahalath, Ishmael's daughter and the sister of Nebaioth (Genesis 28).

name: Nebat
who: An Ephraimite of Zeredah, father of Jeroboam the first king of northern Israel.
key: Nebat is named as the Ephraimite father of Jeroboam, whose mother was Zeruah (1 Kings 11).
Later kings are compared to Jeroboam son of Nebat, who made Israel sin (1 Kings 15; 2 Kings 17).

name: Nebuchadnezzar
who: King of Babylon who conquered Judah, destroyed Jerusalem, and was humbled by the God of Israel.
key: He besieged Jerusalem and carried King Jehoiachin and many others to Babylon (2 Kings 24).
His army burned the temple and Jerusalem after a long siege (2 Kings 25).

name: Nebuzaradan
who: Captain of Nebuchadnezzar's guard who burned Jerusalem and carried its people into exile.
key: He burned the temple, the king's house, and the houses of Jerusalem (2 Kings 25).
He carried the people into exile, leaving some of the poorest behind (2 Kings 25).

name: Nehemiah
who: A leader who returned from Babylon with Zerubbabel, distinct from the later governor Nehemiah.
key: Nehemiah is named among the leaders who came up from exile with Zerubbabel (Ezra 2).
Nehemiah's register of the first returnees lists him again among those leaders (Nehemiah 7).

name: Nehemiah
who: Son of Hacaliah, cupbearer to King Artaxerxes, who became governor of Judah and rebuilt Jerusalem's walls.
key: Hearing that Jerusalem's walls lay broken, Nehemiah wept, fasted, and prayed (Nehemiah 1).
King Artaxerxes granted his request and sent him to rebuild the city (Nehemiah 2).

name: Nehemiah
who: Son of Azbuk and ruler of half the district of Beth-zur, who helped rebuild Jerusalem's wall.
key: As ruler of half the district of Beth-zur, he repaired a section of Jerusalem's wall (Nehemiah 3).
His work reached opposite David's tombs, the artificial pool, and the house of the mighty men (Nehemiah 3).

name: Nemuel
who: A Reubenite, son of Eliab, and brother of Dathan and Abiram.
key: Nemuel is listed as a son of Eliab, of Pallu's clan in the tribe of Reuben (Numbers 26).
His brothers Dathan and Abiram joined Korah's rebellion against Moses and perished (Numbers 26).

name: Nepheg
who: A Levite of the clan of Kohath, son of Izhar and brother of Korah.
key: Nepheg is listed as a son of Izhar, a grandson of Kohath, in the Levite genealogy (Exodus 6).
His brother Korah later led a rebellion against Moses and Aaron (Numbers 16).

name: Ner
who: Benjaminite, son of Abiel, uncle of Saul, and father of Saul's army commander Abner.
key: His son Abner was commander of Saul's army (1 Samuel 14).
Abner son of Ner lay beside Saul when David entered the camp (1 Samuel 26).

name: Neriah
who: Son of Mahseiah and father of Baruch, Jeremiah's scribe, and of Seraiah, a royal officer.
key: Jeremiah gave his land deed to Baruch the son of Neriah for safekeeping (Jeremiah 32).
Baruch the son of Neriah wrote Jeremiah's prophecies on a scroll and read them aloud (Jeremiah 36).

name: Nethanel
who: The son of Zuar and chief of the tribe of Issachar during the wilderness years.
key: Nethanel was appointed to help Moses take the census for Issachar (Numbers 1).
He led Issachar's camp on the east side of the tabernacle (Numbers 2).

name: Nethaniah
who: Son of Elishama of the royal family, known as the father of Ishmael who assassinated Gedaliah.
key: His son Ishmael killed Gedaliah, the governor appointed by Babylon (2 Kings 25).
Johanan warned Gedaliah that Ishmael son of Nethaniah planned to kill him (Jeremiah 40).

name: Nicodemus
who: A Pharisee and ruler of the Jews who came to Jesus by night and later helped bury him.
key: Nicodemus came to Jesus by night, and Jesus taught him about being born again (John 3).
He urged the Pharisees not to condemn Jesus without first giving him a hearing (John 7).

name: Nimrod
who: A son of Cush, the first mighty man on earth and a great hunter, who founded cities in Shinar and Assyria.
key: Nimrod, son of Cush, became the first mighty man on earth, a mighty hunter before the LORD (Genesis 10).
His kingdom began with Babel, Erech, and Accad in the land of Shinar (Genesis 10).

name: Nimshi
who: The grandfather of King Jehu of Israel, who is often called Jehu son of Nimshi.
key: The Lord told Elijah to anoint Jehu son of Nimshi as king over Israel (1 Kings 19).
Elisha sent a prophet to anoint Jehu, son of Jehoshaphat, son of Nimshi (2 Kings 9).

name: Noah
who: Righteous man who built the ark and, with his family, survived the flood.
key: In a corrupt world, Noah found favor with the Lord and was told to build an ark (Genesis 6).
He entered the ark with his family and the animals before the flood came (Genesis 7).

name: Noah
who: One of the five daughters of Zelophehad, who asked Moses for their father's inheritance in Manasseh.
key: Noah is listed among Zelophehad's daughters, since he had no sons (Numbers 26).
She and her sisters asked Moses for their father's inheritance, and the LORD granted it (Numbers 27).

name: Nun
who: An Ephraimite remembered as the father of Joshua.
key: Nun appears in the line of Ephraim as son of Elishama and father of Joshua (1 Chronicles 7).
Joshua is regularly called the son of Nun, from Moses' day onward (Exodus 33; Joshua 1).

name: Obadiah
who: The steward over King Ahab's household who greatly feared the Lord.
key: He hid a hundred of the Lord's prophets in caves and fed them during Jezebel's purge (1 Kings 18).
While searching for grass during the famine, he met Elijah on the road (1 Kings 18).

name: Obadiah
who: A prophet whose short book, the shortest in the Old Testament, announces God's judgment on Edom.
key: Obadiah's vision announces that proud Edom, secure in its rocky heights, will be brought down (Obadiah 1).
He condemns Edom for gloating and violence against its brother Jacob when Jerusalem fell (Obadiah 1).

name: Obed
who: The son of Boaz and Ruth, father of Jesse and grandfather of King David.
key: He was born to Boaz and Ruth, and Naomi cared for him (Ruth 4).
The neighborhood women named him and called him a son born to Naomi (Ruth 4).

name: Ochran
who: A man of Asher whose son Pagiel led the tribe during Israel's wilderness journey.
key: His son Pagiel was named to help Moses take the census for Asher (Numbers 1).
Pagiel son of Ochran led Asher's camp on the north side of the tabernacle (Numbers 2).

name: Oded
who: The father of Azariah, the prophet who urged King Asa of Judah to seek the LORD.
key: The Spirit of God came upon Azariah the son of Oded, who went out to meet King Asa (2 Chronicles 15).
Asa took courage at the prophecy and put away the detestable idols from Judah and Benjamin (2 Chronicles 15).

name: Oded
who: A prophet in Samaria who persuaded Israel's army to free the captives taken from Judah under King Ahaz.
key: Oded met Israel's army returning to Samaria with two hundred thousand captives from Judah (2 Chronicles 28).
He warned that God was angry and that the captives must be sent back (2 Chronicles 28).

name: Og
who: The Amorite king of Bashan, the last of the Rephaim, defeated by Israel.
key: Og came out against Israel at Edrei, and Israel defeated him (Numbers 21).
His iron bed was nine cubits long, showing his great size (Deuteronomy 3).

name: Omar
who: A grandson of Esau through his son Eliphaz, and a chief among the Edomites.
key: Omar was a son of Eliphaz, Esau's firstborn by Adah (Genesis 36).
He is named among the chiefs descended from Eliphaz in Edom (Genesis 36).

name: Omri
who: An army commander who became king of Israel, founded Samaria as its capital, and was father of Ahab.
key: The army made him king after Zimri murdered King Elah, and he besieged Tirzah (1 Kings 16).
He bought the hill of Samaria from Shemer and built the city there (1 Kings 16).

name: Onam
who: A son of Shobal, of the Horite clans who lived in the land of Seir.
key: Onam is listed among the sons of Shobal, a son of Seir the Horite (Genesis 36).
His name is repeated in the genealogy of the people of Seir (1 Chronicles 1).

name: Onam
who: A son of Jerahmeel and his wife Atarah, in the tribe of Judah.
key: Onam was born to Jerahmeel by another wife, Atarah (1 Chronicles 2).
He fathered Shammai and Jada, through whom the Jerahmeelite line continues (1 Chronicles 2).

name: Onan
who: The second son of Judah, whom the Lord put to death for his wickedness.
key: He was born to Judah and the daughter of Shua, a Canaanite (Genesis 38).
Judah told him to raise up offspring for his dead brother Er through Tamar (Genesis 38).

name: Onesimus
who: A slave of Philemon who became a Christian through Paul and was sent back as a brother.
key: Onesimus came to faith through Paul while Paul was in prison (Philemon 1).
Paul sent him back to Philemon, once useless but now useful, as a beloved brother (Philemon 1).

name: Onesiphorus
who: A believer who often refreshed Paul and sought him out in Rome during his imprisonment.
key: Unlike others who turned away, Onesiphorus was not ashamed of Paul's chains (2 Timothy 1).
He searched for Paul in Rome until he found him (2 Timothy 1).

name: Ophir
who: A son of Joktan in the line of Shem, listed in the Table of Nations.
key: Ophir is named among the thirteen sons of Joktan, a descendant of Shem (Genesis 10).
Joktan's sons lived from Mesha toward Sephar, the hill country of the east (Genesis 10).

name: Ophrah
who: A man of Judah, son of Meonothai, in the family line of Othniel, Israel's first judge.
key: Meonothai, of Othniel's family, fathered Ophrah (1 Chronicles 4).
Ophrah is listed among the descendants of Kenaz, the father of Othniel (1 Chronicles 4).

name: Oreb
who: A prince of Midian captured and killed by the Ephraimites during Gideon's victory over Midian.
key: After Gideon's rout of Midian, the Ephraimites captured Oreb and killed him at the rock of Oreb (Judges 7).
They brought the heads of Oreb and Zeeb to Gideon across the Jordan (Judges 7).

name: Oren
who: A son of Jerahmeel, the firstborn of Hezron, in the tribe of Judah.
key: Oren is listed among the sons of Jerahmeel in Judah's genealogy (1 Chronicles 2).
His brothers were Ram, Bunah, Ozem, and Ahijah, and his half-brother was Onam (1 Chronicles 2).

name: Ornan
who: Jebusite whose threshing floor in Jerusalem David bought, later the site of Solomon's temple.
key: The angel bringing plague stopped beside his threshing floor (2 Samuel 24).
He saw the angel while threshing wheat and hid with his sons (1 Chronicles 21).

name: Orpah
who: A Moabite woman, daughter-in-law of Naomi, who returned to her own people instead of going to Bethlehem.
key: Orpah married one of Naomi's sons while the family lived in Moab (Ruth 1).
After her husband died, she set out with Naomi and Ruth toward Judah (Ruth 1).

name: Othniel
who: The son of Kenaz from Judah who became Israel's first judge after Joshua.
key: He captured Kiriath-sepher and received Caleb's daughter Achsah as his wife (Joshua 15).
His capture of the city and marriage to Achsah are recounted again (Judges 1).

name: Ozem
who: The sixth son of Jesse and an older brother of King David.
key: Ozem is named as Jesse's sixth son, with David listed as the seventh (1 Chronicles 2).
His brothers included Eliab, Abinadab, and Shimea, and his sisters were Zeruiah and Abigail (1 Chronicles 2).

name: Ozem
who: A son of Jerahmeel, the firstborn of Hezron, in the tribe of Judah.
key: Ozem is listed among the sons of Jerahmeel in Judah's genealogy (1 Chronicles 2).
His brothers were Ram, Bunah, Oren, and Ahijah, and his half-brother was Onam (1 Chronicles 2).

name: Pagiel
who: The son of Ochran and chief of the tribe of Asher during the wilderness years.
key: Pagiel was appointed to help Moses take the census for Asher (Numbers 1).
He led Asher's camp on the north side of the tabernacle (Numbers 2).

name: Pahath-moab
who: Ancestral head of a large family whose descendants returned from exile with Zerubbabel and with Ezra.
key: The sons of Pahath-moab, through Jeshua and Joab, numbered 2,812 among the returning exiles (Ezra 2).
Eliehoenai son of Zerahiah led two hundred men of this family back with Ezra (Ezra 8).

name: Pallu
who: A son of Reuben, founder of the Palluite clan and ancestor of Dathan and Abiram.
key: Pallu went down to Egypt with Jacob's family as one of Reuben's sons (Genesis 46).
He is listed among the heads of the fathers' houses of Reuben (Exodus 6).

name: Parosh
who: An ancestor whose descendants formed a large family among the exiles who returned from Babylon.
key: The descendants of Parosh numbered 2,172 among those who returned with Zerubbabel (Ezra 2).
Zechariah of the sons of Parosh was registered with 150 men in Ezra's company (Ezra 8).

name: Paruah
who: The father of Jehoshaphat, one of King Solomon's twelve district officers.
key: Paruah is named as father of Jehoshaphat in the list of Solomon's officers (1 Kings 4).
His son Jehoshaphat supplied food for the king's household from Issachar (1 Kings 4).

name: Pasach
who: A man of Asher, son of Japhlet, listed in the genealogy of the tribe of Asher.
key: The sons of Japhlet were Pasach, Bimhal, and Ashvath (1 Chronicles 7).
Japhlet was a son of Heber, the son of Asher's son Beriah (1 Chronicles 7).

name: Pashhur
who: A priest, son of Malchijah, whose large family of descendants returned from exile and served in Jerusalem.
key: Pashhur appears as an ancestor of Adaiah, a priest living in Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 9).
More than twelve hundred of Pashhur's descendants returned from Babylon with Zerubbabel (Ezra 2).

name: Paul
who: Pharisee from Tarsus who persecuted the church, then became an apostle to the Gentiles and wrote many New Testament letters.
key: As a young man named Saul, he approved of the stoning of Stephen (Acts 7).
The risen Jesus appeared to him on the road to Damascus, and he was converted (Acts 9).

name: Pedahzur
who: A man of Manasseh whose son Gamaliel led the tribe during Israel's wilderness journey.
key: His son Gamaliel was named to help Moses take the census for Manasseh (Numbers 1).
Gamaliel son of Pedahzur led Manasseh's camp on the west side of the tabernacle (Numbers 2).

name: Pedaiah
who: A Benjaminite, son of Kolaiah and father of Joed, in the ancestry of Sallu of Jerusalem.
key: Sallu son of Meshullam is traced through Joed, Pedaiah, Kolaiah, Maaseiah, and Ithiel to Jeshaiah (Nehemiah 11).
These Benjaminites were among the people who lived in Jerusalem, the holy city (Nehemiah 11).

name: Pekah
who: A captain who killed King Pekahiah and reigned over Israel in Samaria, allying with Syria against Judah.
key: He conspired against Pekahiah, killed him, and reigned in his place for twenty years (2 Kings 15).
Tiglath-pileser of Assyria captured many of his cities, and Hoshea assassinated him (2 Kings 15).

name: Pekahiah
who: A son of Menahem who reigned over Israel two years before his officer Pekah assassinated him.
key: Pekahiah succeeded his father Menahem as king of Israel (2 Kings 15).
He reigned two years in Samaria and did evil, following Jeroboam's sins (2 Kings 15).

name: Pelaliah
who: A priest in the ancestry of Adaiah, who served in the house of the LORD after the exile.
key: Adaiah son of Jeroham, son of Pelaliah, son of Amzi, is listed among the priests in Jerusalem (Nehemiah 11).
His line is traced back through Zechariah and Pashhur to Malchijah (Nehemiah 11).

name: Pelatiah
who: A son of Benaiah and leader in Jerusalem who died suddenly while Ezekiel prophesied against the city's wicked leaders.
key: Ezekiel saw Pelatiah among twenty-five men at the temple gate giving wicked counsel (Ezekiel 11).
While Ezekiel prophesied, Pelatiah died, and Ezekiel fell on his face crying out to God (Ezekiel 11).

name: Peleg
who: Son of Eber, in whose days the earth was divided; an ancestor of Abraham and of Jesus.
key: He was named Peleg because in his days the earth was divided (Genesis 10).
He fathered Reu at thirty and lived 209 years more (Genesis 11).
